swift_specific_fixes.swift_fix: var components = URLComponents(string: "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript"); components?.path = "/" + transcriptID.addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: .urlPathAllowed) ?? transcriptID; guard let pollURL = components?.url else { throw TranscriptionError.invalidTranscriptID }
swift_specific_fixes.exploitability: HIGH - Path traversal via ../ or query injection via ?redirect=evil.com
swift_specific_fixes.swift_rationale: URLComponents provides RFC 3986 compliant encoding, automatically escaping reserved characters. Direct interpolation bypasses percent-encoding, allowing attackers to inject path separators and query delimiters.

swift_specific_fixes.swift_fix: let encodedID = id.addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: .urlPathAllowed) ?? id; guard let url = URL(string: baseURL)?.appendingPathComponent("transcript").appendingPathComponent(encodedID) else { throw TranscriptionError.invalidURL }
swift_specific_fixes.exploitability: HIGH - Double URL encoding attacks or path traversal if baseURL is attacker-controlled
swift_specific_fixes.swift_rationale: URL.appendingPathComponent() normalizes path separators and prevents traversal sequences. String interpolation allows '../' to escape path context.

swift_specific_fixes.exploitability: MEDIUM - Path traversal to overwrite arbitrary files in app container
swift_specific_fixes.swift_rationale: MLX model downloads from remote sources require both path traversal filtering AND URL-safe construction. Combining validation with appendingPathComponent() provides defense in depth.

swift_specific_fixes.exploitability: MEDIUM - Memory dump analysis, crash logs, or debugger attachment can extract key
swift_specific_fixes.swift_rationale: Swift String uses copy-on-write and can exist in multiple memory locations. SecureString with ~Copyable prevents accidental copies, explicit memory zeroing prevents extraction from crash dumps.

swift_specific_fixes.exploitability: MEDIUM - Key persists in memory for lifetime of configuration object
swift_specific_fixes.swift_rationale: String? properties retain value in heap until deallocated. SecureString provides explicit lifecycle management with RAII-style cleanup via deinit.

swift_specific_fixes.exploitability: MEDIUM - Key extractable from process memory via ptrace or crash dumps
swift_specific_fixes.swift_rationale: let constants may be optimized into binary read-only section. SecureString ensures key material is never in a predictable memory location and is actively cleared after use.

swift_specific_considerations.arc_implications: Swift ARC means String copies persist until last reference gone. SecureString must use ~Copyable to prevent implicit copies.
swift_specific_considerations.keychain_integration: Keychain returns Data or String. Convert to SecureString immediately after retrieval, never store String property.
swift_specific_considerations.concurrency_safety: SecureString operations should be isolated to actors or use locks for thread-safe access to the buffer.
swift_specific_considerations.crash_reporting: Swift crash logs may include heap dumps. Zeroing memory in deinit reduces key exposure window.
